glossary.Partial thrombosis: A clot that narrows but does not completely block the artery.
glossary.Coronary blood flow: Blood flow through the arteries supplying the heart muscle.
glossary.Ischaemic heart disease: Heart disease caused by narrowed coronary arteries reducing blood supply to the heart.
glossary.Central chest pain: Pain in the middle of the chest, behind the breastbone.
glossary.New onset: Symptoms that have only just started.
glossary.Tachycardia: Heart rate above 100 beats per minute.
glossary.Heart failure: The heart cannot pump enough blood to meet the body's needs.
glossary.Radiation: Pain spreading from where it starts to another area, such as arm or jaw.
glossary.Palpitations: An unpleasant awareness of your own heartbeat.
glossary.ECG: Electrocardiogram: a recording of the heart's electrical activity.
glossary.Risk stratification: Sorting patients by how likely they are to have a bad outcome, to guide treatment.
glossary.Early invasive management: Doing coronary angiography and treating blockages within days rather than with drugs alone.
glossary.Conservative management: Treating with medicines and monitoring rather than a procedure.
glossary.Aspirin: An antiplatelet drug that stops platelets clumping on a plaque.
glossary.Antiplatelet: A drug that stops platelets sticking together to form clots.
glossary.Dual antiplatelet therapy: Aspirin plus a second antiplatelet drug, usually for 12 months after ACS.
glossary.Anticoagulation: Drugs that slow the clotting cascade so clots do not grow.
glossary.SpO2: Oxygen saturation measured by a finger probe.
glossary.MI: Myocardial infarction: heart muscle death from a blocked coronary artery.
glossary.Beta-blocker: Drug that slows the heart and lowers its oxygen needs.
glossary.ACE inhibitor: Drug that blocks angiotensin II formation, lowering BP and protecting the heart.
glossary.Statin: A drug that lowers LDL cholesterol and stabilises plaques.
glossary.Atherosclerotic plaque: A fatty, fibrous build-up in an artery wall that narrows it.
glossary.Plaque erosion: Loss of the lining cells over a plaque, which can trigger a clot without a full rupture.
glossary.Platelet aggregation: Platelets sticking together to start a clot.
glossary.Propagate: For a clot, to keep growing along the vessel.
glossary.Coagulation cascade: The chain of clotting factors that ends in fibrin, which forms a stable clot.
glossary.Licence: A driving licence; Group 1 for cars and motorbikes, Group 2 for lorries and buses.
glossary.Complementary: Working in different ways that add to each other.
glossary.LMWH: Low molecular weight heparin, an injected anticoagulant such as enoxaparin.
glossary.P2Y12 inhibitor: An antiplatelet that blocks the platelet ADP receptor, such as clopidogrel or ticagrelor.
